wine.name: Grüner Veltliner Ried Hund
wine.classification: Reserve, the fuller tier of the Weinviertel DAC
wine.sites: The Hundsleiten above Stetten, on the Bisamberg ridge just north of Vienna, which gives the wine its name: flysch soils of clay and sandstone layers laced with quartz, planted by the founder in the years after 1978.
wine.making: The grapes are selected in the vineyard and picked in the middle of October. After some eight hours on their skins they are pressed gently in a pneumatic press, and the wine is fermented and raised half in large wooden casks and half in stainless steel, as the house describes it.
wine.glass: Ripe pear, yellow apple and white pepper over a stony grip; powerful and full for a Grüner Veltliner, with lively acidity and a long, peppery finish.
wine.ageing: Ready a year after the harvest, it fills out over three to five years, and a ripe vintage holds for ten.
wine.serve: 10 to 12 degrees Celsius; no need to decant, though a young bottle opens with air; a white wine glass with a generous bowl.

label.means: The appellation's fuller tier: dry, at least thirteen per cent alcohol, with a hint of oak or botrytis allowed.
The vineyard name, short for the Hundsleiten above Stetten, where all its grapes grow.
Austria's own white grape, and the one grape the Weinviertel DAC admits.

records.table: Pfaffl's Grüner Veltliner Hund is a Weinviertel DAC Reserve from the Hundsleiten above Stetten, just north of Vienna. Powerful for the grape, with ripe pear and white pepper over a stony grip, it stands up to roast chicken or a schnitzel.
records.story: Before 1978 the Pfaffl farm at Stetten, on the Bisamberg just north of Vienna, grew cereals and kept pigs and cows, with only a small plot of vines and an old cellar. That year a young couple of the family married and took it over, and they set out to make wine the whole of the business. Among the first things the founder did was plant Grüner Veltliner on the Hundsleiten, a slope of flysch above the village, and the wine of that slope, named Hund for it, became the house's calling card. In 2003 the Weinviertel became Austria's first DAC, an appellation for peppery Grüner Veltliner alone, and from the 2009 vintage it added a Reserve tier for riper, fuller wines; the Hund is labelled a Weinviertel DAC Reserve. The estate grew from that one slope to vineyards across the southern Weinviertel and in Vienna, and the next generation of the family joined the founders in the cellar. Low yields, much hand work and a late harvest, as the house puts it, give the Hund its weight. For a sommelier it is a lesson in the Reserve style: Grüner Veltliner with the pepper of the classic tier and the body to stand beside a main course.

others.name: Grüner Veltliner Hommage
others.note: A Weinviertel DAC Reserve from very old vines on the Kirchenberg of Grossebersdorf, fermented with wild yeasts in acacia casks.

others.name: Grüner Veltliner Haiden
others.note: A Weinviertel DAC from the Haid, on deep loess over a rocky subsoil.

traps: R&A Pfaffl, the house of the Hund, is not the separate Heinz and Theresia Pfaffl estate in the same village of Stetten.
Hund means dog in German, but on this label it is the vineyard: the Hundsleiten above Stetten, not a brand name.

cards.front: Pfaffl's Hund: which vineyard gives it its name, and on what rock does it grow?
cards.back: The Hundsleiten above Stetten, on flysch of clay and sandstone layers laced with quartz.

cards.front: What did the Pfaffl farm at Stetten produce before 1978?
cards.back: Cereals, pigs and cows, with only a little wine; the couple who took it over that year made it a winery.

questions.q: A guest sees Weinviertel DAC Reserve on Pfaffl's Grüner Veltliner Hund. What does the word Reserve promise?
opts: A dry, fuller wine of at least thirteen per cent alcohol
A wine aged three years before release
A sweet wine of late picked grapes
A blend of Grüner Veltliner and Riesling
questions.exp: Reserve is the Weinviertel DAC's fuller tier: dry, at least thirteen per cent alcohol, with a hint of oak or botrytis allowed; it asks for no long ageing, and the DAC admits Grüner Veltliner alone.

questions.q: In which year did a young couple take over the Pfaffl farm at Stetten and begin turning it into a winery?
questions.exp: They married and took over the mixed farm in 1978; 2003 is the year the Weinviertel became Austria's first DAC, long after the Hundsleiten was planted.

sources.title: Pfaffl: HUND Weinviertel Reserve, fact sheet
Discover Germany: R&A Pfaffl winery, the Hund

report: The lint holds the name to the plan's words, Grüner Veltliner Ried Hund, but the house and its retailers print Grüner Veltliner Weinviertel DAC Reserve Hund, with no Ried; I propose a swap of the wine's name alone to Grüner Veltliner Hund.

The plan's doubt over the flagship: the house calls the Hund its prototypical Grüner Veltliner and an English feature on the house is built around it, so the pick stands; Hommage is the old vine selection in others.

Wine Enthusiast's European Winery of the Year, the house's part in founding the Weinviertel DAC and the founder's nickname Mr. Veltliner each rest on one source and are left out; so is the year the Hund was first labelled a Reserve.
The older name of the wine, Hundsleiten Sandtal, appears in a Falstaff listing of 1999 and a Dutch retailer's page; it is left out of the record for want of room among the five sources.
The region record calls Pfaffl the southern Weinviertel's leading estate, a judgement the record does not repeat; the house is not among the thirteen founders of the ÖTW's Weinviertel association.

wine.name: Grüner Veltliner Ried Bürsting
wine.sites: The Bürsting, a high plateau at the end of a cellar lane in Poysdorf, on deep, moist loam, with vines planted in the early 1960s; the gravel of the Sauberg lies just behind it.
wine.making: Picked by hand into small crates in October, the grapes rest about a day on their skins before pressing. The must is settled briefly and fermented with wild yeasts, partly in used 500 litre barrels and partly in small steel tanks, and the wine is bottled in the late spring after the harvest.
wine.glass: Yellow pear, quince and white pepper over a dense, creamy texture; broad and savoury, with ripe acidity and a long, peppery close.
wine.ageing: Approachable within two years of the harvest, it gains depth over five to eight, and a strong vintage lasts a decade or more.
wine.serve: 10 to 12 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for half an hour to let it open; a white wine glass with a generous bowl.

label.means: The single vineyard; Austrian law asks for the word Ried before a vineyard's name.
Organic: the house's own sheets describe the Bürsting as organically grown.

records.table: Ebner-Ebenauer's Grüner Veltliner Ried Bürsting comes from a loam plateau above a cellar lane in Poysdorf, from vines planted in the early 1960s. Fermented with wild yeasts, partly in old barrels, it is dense and peppery, a white for roast pork.
records.story: The family behind the house has grown wine around Poysdorf, in the north east of the Weinviertel, for many generations, fourteen by its own count, and its cellar, cut six metres into the ground on three levels, is held to be some four hundred years old. The farm above it burnt almost to the ground in 1945, at the end of the Second World War, and was rebuilt; grandparents who had studied in France and Italy brought something of the Mediterranean into the new house, as the family tells it. In 2007 a young couple, one of them heir to the family's vines, launched the wines under their joined names, Ebner-Ebenauer, and set about bottling each parcel on its own. They farmed organically and let the must run into the cellar by gravity, without pumps. In 2022 Falstaff named the couple its Winemakers of the Year. The house was among the thirteen founders of the Weinviertel association of the ÖTW, the traditional estates that classify Austria's Erste Lagen, and its Sauberg and Hermannschachern carry that rank. The Bürsting, older vines on the deeper loam in front of the Sauberg, shows the warmth and weight Grüner Veltliner can find at Poysdorf.

others.name: Grüner Veltliner Ried Sauberg 1ÖTW
others.note: An Erste Lage of the ÖTW behind the Bürsting, where gravel meets the loam, from vines planted in the early 1960s.

others.name: Grüner Veltliner Ried Hermannschachern 1ÖTW
others.note: A second Erste Lage of Poysdorf among the house's classified single vineyard wines.

traps: The Bürsting is a single Ried wine but not an ÖTW Erste Lage: the house's classified sites are the Sauberg and the Hermannschachern.
Ebner-Ebenauer is one estate whose name joins two family names, not two houses of Poysdorf.

cards.front: Ebner-Ebenauer's Bürsting: what soil, and when were its vines planted?
cards.back: Deep, moist loam on a plateau above a Poysdorf cellar lane, with vines planted in the early 1960s.

cards.front: What befell the Ebner-Ebenauer family's farm at Poysdorf in 1945?
cards.back: It burnt almost to the ground and was rebuilt after the war.

questions.q: A guest asks how Ebner-Ebenauer ferments its Grüner Veltliner Ried Bürsting. Which answer fits?
opts: With wild yeasts, partly in used 500 litre barrels
With cultured yeasts in new small barriques
In concrete eggs after a month on the skins
In stainless steel alone, bottled within weeks
questions.exp: The house ferments the Bürsting spontaneously, partly in used 500 litre barrels and partly in small steel tanks; there is no new barrique, and steel is only part of it.

questions.q: In which year were the wines of the Poysdorf estate first released under the name Ebner-Ebenauer?
questions.exp: The Ebner-Ebenauer label dates from 2007; 1945 is the fire that destroyed the family farm, and 2022 the year Falstaff named the couple Winemakers of the Year.

sources.title: Falstaff: Winemaker of the Year, the power couple Ebner-Ebenauer
Wein.plus: ÖTW found an association in the Weinviertel with thirteen founding wineries

report: No source names a single flagship of the house: the Bürsting is its long standing single Ried Grüner Veltliner, reviewed by Falstaff since at least 2011, but the ÖTW Erste Lage wines Sauberg and Hermannschachern head the classified range; the checker may weigh a swap of the wine to Grüner Veltliner Ried Sauberg 1ÖTW.

The appellation is uncertain: Falstaff lists the 2011 as Weinviertel DAC Reserve Bürsting, while a tasting note on the 2015 gives Niederösterreich; the record says Niederösterreich and prints no appellation term on the label, and the checker should confirm against a recent label.
Organic farming from the 2016 vintage and the conversion to biodynamics rest on one importer and are left out; the ÖTW association's founding year is in the Zull record.
The Sekt the plan mentions was not found in the sources read and is left out of others; the region record's Poysdorf as the Sekt town is not repeated.

wine.name: Grüner Veltliner Ried Äussere Bergen
wine.classification: Reserve of the Weinviertel DAC; an Erste Lage of the ÖTW, printed 1ÖTW
wine.sites: The Äussere Bergen, the south easternmost vineyard of Schrattenthal at about 280 metres, sheltered to the west by the Hüttberg: weathered granite of the Manhartsberg under a thin cover of loess.
wine.making: Picked by hand early in October, the grapes rest some eighteen hours on their skins before pressing. The wine is raised in large wooden casks, in some vintages with a share in steel, and the house gives it about fifteen months before bottling.
wine.glass: Ripe apricot, baked apple and white pepper over a salty, stony grip; velvety and full, with fresh acidity and a long finish touched with tobacco.
wine.ageing: Broad and open two years after the harvest, it drinks well for eight to ten years from a ripe vintage.
wine.serve: 10 to 12 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for half an hour; a white wine glass with a generous bowl.

label.means: The appellation's fuller tier: dry, at least thirteen per cent alcohol, with a hint of oak allowed.
An Erste Lage, a site classified by the ÖTW, the association of Austria's traditional wine estates.
The vineyard's name, the outer hills, the south easternmost slope of Schrattenthal.

records.table: Zull's Grüner Veltliner Ried Äussere Bergen is a Weinviertel DAC Reserve from granite under loess at Schrattenthal near Retz, in the cool west of the region. Raised in large casks, it is ripe and velvety with white pepper, so pour it with roast veal.
records.story: Schrattenthal, a small town on the edge of the Waldviertel, appears in a document of 1220, and the house at number nine is where the Zull story begins: a great grandfather of the family married into it, at a time when wine was one crop among many on a mixed farm. In the 1980s a later generation gave up the rest and turned the farm wholly to wine, as the house recounts. Its vineyards lie on weathered granite of the Manhartsberg under a thin coat of loess, and cold winds from the higher Waldviertel to the west cool the grapes as they ripen. In 2003 the Weinviertel became Austria's first DAC, for Grüner Veltliner alone, and from the 2009 vintage a Reserve tier followed for fuller wines; the Äussere Bergen is the house's Reserve from one slope. In 2024 Zull was among the thirteen estates that founded the Weinviertel association of the ÖTW, which ranks the Äussere Bergen an Erste Lage. For a sommelier it shows the western Weinviertel: granite, cool nights and Grüner Veltliner of ripe fruit and firm line.

others.name: Riesling Ried Innere Bergen
others.note: Riesling from the inner hills of Schrattenthal, which the ÖTW names among the village's key sites.

others.name: Grüner Veltliner Schrattenthal
others.note: The village wine, a Weinviertel DAC from the house's parcels around Schrattenthal.

traps: Zull's granite lies in the far west by the Manhartsberg; most of the Weinviertel grows on loess, sand and gravel, so this is not the region's usual soil.
The Äussere Bergen is a single vineyard of Schrattenthal, not a village of its own, and the wine carries the Reserve tier.

cards.front: Zull's Äussere Bergen: what lies under the vines, and how high is the slope?
cards.back: Weathered granite under a thin cover of loess, at about 280 metres.

cards.front: Zull's home of Schrattenthal near Retz: when is it first recorded in a document?

questions.q: A guest asks why Zull's Grüner Veltliner Ried Äussere Bergen may show a trace of wood. Which reason fits?
opts: It is a Reserve, which may show a hint of oak
It is a classic tier wine aged in new barriques
It is labelled outside the DAC as a table wine
Its grapes are dried on mats before pressing
questions.exp: The Weinviertel DAC allows a hint of oak in a Reserve but none in the classic tier; the Äussere Bergen is a DAC Reserve raised in large wooden casks.

questions.q: In which year did Zull join twelve other estates in founding the Weinviertel association of the ÖTW?
questions.exp: The association was founded in 2024; 2003 was the first Weinviertel DAC and 2009 the vintage that brought its Reserve tier.

sources.title: Weingut Zull: Grüner Veltliner Äussere Bergen Weinviertel DAC Reserve 1ÖTW
Wine Enthusiast: Zull 2021 Ried Äussere Bergen Reserve Grüner Veltliner
Meininger: the ÖTW welcome the Weinviertel

report: The region record's granite and loess for the house is confirmed for the Äussere Bergen by the house's own page: granite at about 280 metres under loess.

Founded is empty: the house dates its turn to wine alone to the 1980s and elsewhere to some forty seven years ago, and gives no founding year; the great grandfather who married into the house is named on its page without dates, so he is not named here.
The vessels vary by vintage: the house and Falstaff give large wooden casks, a Decanter note on 2015 half large oak and half steel; the record says large casks with a share in steel in some vintages.
The ÖTW association's year, 2024, rests on Meininger and Wein.plus; its first vintage of Reserve, 2009, on the Austrian wine body's press note.
Whether the wine is fermented with wild yeasts was not found, so it is not said.

wine.name: Grüner Veltliner Ried Laa 8000
wine.classification: Reserve of the Weinviertel DAC; an Erste Lage of the ÖTW, printed 1ÖTW
wine.sites: The Ried Laa at Hohenwarth, high on the western edge of the Weinviertel at about 400 metres: a very chalky soil with white lines of lime plain on the surface, planted at about eight thousand vines to every ten thousand square metres.
wine.making: Fermented with wild yeasts in stainless steel and raised in steel for some ten months, so that site and grape alone shape it. The close planting forces the roots deep against drought and keeps each vine's crop small, which the house holds is the source of the wine's concentration.
wine.glass: Lime, green pear and white pepper over a chalky, salty core; taut and juicy, with lively acidity, close concentration and a long, peppery finish.
wine.ageing: Tight in its first two years, it opens over three to six and lasts ten or more from a strong vintage.
wine.serve: 10 to 12 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for half an hour; a white wine glass with a generous bowl.

label.means: The planting density: about eight thousand vines to every ten thousand square metres in the Ried Laa.
An Erste Lage, a site classified by the ÖTW, the association of Austria's traditional wine estates.
The appellation's fuller tier: dry and at least thirteen per cent alcohol.

records.table: Setzer's Grüner Veltliner Ried Laa 8000 is named for the eight thousand vines planted to every ten thousand square metres in a chalky Erste Lage at Hohenwarth. Fermented with wild yeasts and kept in steel, it is taut, salty and peppery, made for trout or veal.
records.story: Wine has been made at Hohenwarth, on the high western edge of the Weinviertel, since at least 1360, the house recounts, and the Setzer family has worked here since 1705, by its own account. For most of those centuries the estate was a mixed farm: a family photograph of 1909 shows a farmer and his wife with their three children, the youngest the great grandfather of the youngest generation of the house. Only in 2001 did the family give up crops and livestock and become a wine estate alone. In 2003 the Weinviertel became Austria's first DAC, for Grüner Veltliner alone, and from the 2009 vintage a Reserve tier followed for fuller wines. On their chalkiest site, the Ried Laa, the family had planted Grüner Veltliner at about eight thousand vines to every ten thousand square metres, more than twice the density usual in the region, and they named the wine for the figure. Setzer is one of the thirteen estates that founded the Weinviertel association of the ÖTW, which ranks the Laa an Erste Lage. The house calls the 8000 its flagship, and for a sommelier it is the case for dense planting in a dry land.

others.name: Grüner Veltliner Große Reserve Ried Laa
others.note: From the same site, in the fullest tier of the Weinviertel DAC, held longer in the cellar than a Reserve.

others.name: Grüner Veltliner Ried Kronberg
others.note: A second Weinviertel DAC Reserve from a single Ried of Hohenwarth.

others.name: Grüner Veltliner Hohenwarth
others.note: The village wine, fermented with wild yeasts and kept in stainless steel.

traps: The 8000 is the number of vines to every ten thousand square metres in the Ried Laa, not a vintage, a bottle count or an altitude.
The 8000 is a Reserve, not the Große Reserve: Setzer makes a Große Reserve from the same Ried Laa, held longer before release.

cards.front: Setzer's Ried Laa 8000: what does the figure on the label stand for?
cards.back: About eight thousand vines to every ten thousand square metres, planted close to force the roots deep.

cards.front: Since which year has the Setzer family worked at Hohenwarth, by its own account?

questions.q: A guest asks why Setzer planted its Ried Laa so closely, at eight thousand vines to every ten thousand square metres. Which reason does the house give?
opts: Deep roots and small crops in a dry land
Shade for the grapes in hot summers
Shelter from spring frost on the valley floor
Rows close enough for harvesting by machine
questions.exp: The house says close planting forces the roots deep against drought and limits each vine's crop; it says nothing of shade or frost, and dense rows do not suit machines.

questions.q: Which change came to the Setzer estate at Hohenwarth in 2001?
opts: It gave up crops and livestock to make wine alone
It passed out of the family
It became Austria's first DAC estate
It joined the ÖTW's Weinviertel association
questions.exp: In 2001 the family ended its mixed farming and became a wine estate alone; the ÖTW's Weinviertel association came only in 2024, and the house has stayed in the family since 1705.

sources.title: Weingut Setzer: Grüner Veltliner Weinviertel DAC Reserve Ried Laa 8000 1ÖTW
Falstaff: Setzer 2019 Weinviertel DAC Reserve Ried Laa 8000

report: The plan's question is answered: the house's own page says 8000 is the planting density, eight thousand vines to every ten thousand square metres in the Ried Laa, and calls the wine the flagship of the estate.
The label reads Grüner Veltliner Weinviertel DAC Reserve Ried Laa 8000, with 1ÖTW; the record's name drops the appellation words, which stand in the appellation field.
The founding year 1705 is the house's own and an importer's; one retailer gives 1730, so the story hedges it as the family's account.
The steel and the ten months rest on Falstaff's sheet for 2019 and the importer's note of wild yeast in steel; the house's pages read did not say.
The year the 8000 was planted (more than twenty years ago by the house's page) and a once disputed use of the figure on the DAC label, reported only by a writer's own site, are left out.

wine.name: Grüner Veltliner Weinviertel DAC
wine.classification: The classic tier of the Weinviertel DAC, beneath Reserve and Große Reserve
wine.sites: Parcels in and around Röschitz on the eastern slopes of the Manhartsberg, at 280 to 340 metres, on loess and weathered primary rock with granite among it.
wine.making: The grapes are pressed gently in a pneumatic press and the must is fermented in stainless steel at a controlled twenty degrees or so. The wine then rests on its lees in steel for some weeks before an early bottling; the rules of the classic tier allow no taste of oak or botrytis.
wine.glass: Green apple, yellow grapefruit peel and white pepper; light and lively, with crisp acidity, a faint bitter twist of lemon pith and a clean, dry finish.
wine.ageing: Made to be drunk young, within one to three years of the harvest, while its pepper and freshness last.
wine.serve: 8 to 10 degrees Celsius; no need to decant; a white wine glass.

label.means: Austria's first DAC, for Grüner Veltliner alone: dry, peppery and with no taste of oak.
The village of the house and its vineyards, which may follow the grape's name on the label.
Organic: the family has farmed its vineyards organically since 2013, by its own account.

records.table: Gruber Röschitz's Grüner Veltliner Weinviertel DAC is the appellation's classic tier from loess and granite around Röschitz on the Manhartsberg. Fermented cool in steel and bottled young, it is light, dry and full of white pepper, a glass for the Heuriger table.
records.story: The Gruber family has farmed at Röschitz, on the eastern slopes of the Manhartsberg in the north west of the Weinviertel, for more than two hundred years, as it tells the story, and for most of that time its wine was made largely for the household. A later generation built the farm into an estate centred on Grüner Veltliner, which fills about half of its vineyards. In 2003 the Weinviertel became Austria's first DAC, created for peppery Grüner Veltliner alone; a Weinviertel DAC with no Reserve on its label is the classic tier, dry, fresh and free of any taste of oak or botrytis. In 2012 three of six siblings took over their parents' farm, sharing the vineyards, the cellar and the selling between them, and from 2013 they farmed organically. Röschitz is not typical Weinviertel ground: where most of the region grows on gravel, sand and loess, the soils here are poor primary rock with granite under shallow loess. Gruber Röschitz was also among the thirteen founders of the Weinviertel association of the ÖTW. For a sommelier its DAC wine is the measure of the classic tier: the plain, peppery Grüner Veltliner the appellation was made for.

others.name: Grüner Veltliner Ried Reipersberg
others.note: A Weinviertel DAC from a terraced south slope of granite, with vines up to about sixty years old, by the house's account.

others.name: Grüner Veltliner Ried Mühlberg
others.note: A Weinviertel DAC Reserve from the hill above the old Röschitz mill.

traps: A Weinviertel DAC with no Reserve on the label is the classic tier: at most six grams of sugar to the litre, with no taste of oak or botrytis.
Gruber Röschitz is one family estate of the village of Röschitz; the place name is part of the house's name, not a second producer.

cards.front: Gruber Röschitz: on what soils do the vines around Röschitz grow?
cards.back: Poor primary rock with granite, under shallow loess, on the eastern slopes of the Manhartsberg.

cards.front: In which year did three Gruber siblings take over their parents' farm at Röschitz?

questions.q: A guest asks whether Gruber Röschitz's Grüner Veltliner Weinviertel DAC has seen oak. What is true?
opts: No: the classic tier allows no taste of oak
Yes: it spends a year in new barriques
Yes: it is raised in old acacia casks
No: it is a sparkling wine made in tank
questions.exp: The classic Weinviertel DAC must show no oak or botrytis, and the house ferments it in stainless steel; a hint of oak is allowed only in a Reserve.

questions.q: From which year has the Gruber family at Röschitz farmed its vineyards organically?
questions.exp: The siblings took over in 2012 and turned to organic farming from 2013; 2003 is the year of the first Weinviertel DAC.

sources.title: Gruber Röschitz: Falstaff on the young Weinviertel

report: Thin region rule: the house is a family estate known for a well made, widely poured DAC wine rather than a single famous bottling, and the record says so; the pick stands, no swap to Weinrieder proposed.

The label form has moved: older vintages print Weinviertel DAC Klassik Grüner Veltliner, recent ones Weinviertel DAC Grüner Veltliner Röschitz with no Klassik; the lint holds the name to the plan's words, and the checker may wish a swap of the wine's name to Grüner Veltliner Röschitz.
Founded is empty: one regional chamber article gives 1814 for the family's farming at Röschitz, a retailer only more than two hundred years; the story says the latter, as the family tells it.

The steel fermentation, the temperature, the lees and the 280 to 340 metres come from the house's sheet for its DAC wine; that the wine was also bottled young rests on its one to three year window on the house's own pages.
The family's work for Stift Altenburg and Schloss Maissau is the house's claim alone and is left out.
